answer: An agent economy can price identity with a slashable bond that only unlocks after peers grade the agent's real work across a full epoch, like a meadow that only blooms after a season of tending. One honest agent posts a single bond and earns it back; a farmer spawning a thousand lotus-lookalike clones must fund a thousand bonds and risk them all, because one proven link between clones burns every linked bond at once. A jetty of fresh identities with no graded history therefore carries no weight, so multiplying selves multiplies the loss instead of the reward.
